historical_record.description: A contract was recorded with William E. Roeder for concrete and carpenter work on a six-storey and basement building, at $19,085.

The Board of Permit Appeals upheld the Zoning Administrator's determination that conversion of the Cornell Hotel at 715 Bush Street from mixed residential and tourist use to all tourist use requires conditional use authorization.
Cornell Hotel was at 715 Bush Street.
The building was a 31-room residential hotel (group housing), proposed for conversion above the ground floor to a 58-unit tourist hotel.
The City Planning Commission refused, 4-1, to let the Cornell Hotel convert from a 31-room residential hotel to a 58-unit tourist hotel above the ground floor (Motion 13659).

The Board of Permit Appeals overruled the Zoning Administrator's determination as to the number of hotel rooms at the Cornell Hotel at 715 Bush Street designated for residential use, reducing the number from 31 to 24, on rehearing.

The Board of Permit Appeals upheld the Zoning Administrator's determination that conditional use authorization is required to convert the rooms at the Cornell Hotel at 715 Bush Street from residential to tourist use, on rehearing.
By 21 April 1994 the Board of Permit Appeals had reduced to 24, from 31, the units of the Cornell Hotel that had to remain residential.

The Board of Permit Appeals upheld the denial of the hotel conversion application for the Cornell Hotel at 715 Bush Street to full tourist use, for failure to meet the requirement of the Hotel Conversion Ordinance Section 41.13(d).

The Board of Permit Appeals set aside its decision of May 3, 1995 and overruled the department, granting the permit to convert seven rooms from residential to tourist use at the Cornell Hotel, 715 Bush Street, as required by a peremptory writ of mandamus.
